intended_use.user: one internal FlyRank content reviewer, ~50 review slots per week
intended_use.decision: order in which pages get a human look

ranking_quality.claim: not worse than the Week-4 rule, plausibly somewhat better; the pooled gap sits inside the fold-to-fold spread (Week 6)

decay_refresh.content_age_gradient: none observable across quintiles in this slice
decay_refresh.update_recency_gradient: not testable -- days_since_last_update is bimodal with near-empty middle buckets

cost_value.monetary_value_reason: cpc is 0 on 76% of rows and search_volume on 37%
cost_value.recovery_rate_reason: no intervention was assigned; requires a held-out control set

human_review.always_on: CHECK_TOPIC_SENSITIVITY -- topic is not in the feature set, so a human is the only control
no_go: auto-publishing any title, meta or body text
acting while the analytics-mismatch flag is open
page-by-page work while one client dominates the queue
scoring pages below the volume floor
any client-facing number, forecast or projected uplift
using the score to evaluate a writer, agency or team
running a queue older than 45 days
reading before/after on reviewed pages as an effect

checks.what it would mean: the thing being ranked changed; precision@K is no longer comparable month to month
if it falls below the Week-4 rule, ship the rule -- it is free and needs no fitting
the queue has become one client's worklist; portfolio framing no longer honest
too low = churn/noise; too high = the queue is frozen and nothing is being worked
the LABEL is defined against these -- drift here changes the question, not just the answer
an input is degrading; review flags start firing on noise
survivorship is growing; rates in the playbook describe an increasingly filtered set

checks.check: reviewer accept rate of queue rows
checks.what it would mean: the only check that tests the queue against human judgment -- must be captured from week one

retrain_triggers: any check red, or the same check amber two months running
new client above ~10% of eligible pages
band norms move more than 20% (this changes the label, not just the inputs)
schema or definition change in any input column
more than 90 days since the last fit
monitoring.caveat: thresholds are set from a single observation and are hypotheses until a second month exists

limits.measured as: largest client = 40% of the universe, 78% of the top 200
limits.what it forbids: the queue largely describes one client's pages; a portfolio-level claim is not supported

limits.measured as: 1,683 pages (15%) dropped below the volume floor in the later window
limits.what it forbids: pages that collapsed in traffic are excluded from every rate above, in both directions

limits.measured as: persisted_shortfall is a defined rule, not a reviewed outcome
limits.what it forbids: measures that a gap stayed open; says nothing about whether it was fixable

limits.measured as: avg_position is a 90-day average overlapping the outcome window
limits.what it forbids: Week 5 refit without position: PR-AUC moved ~0.03 -- bounded, not the source of the result

limits.measured as: per-fold P@50 sd = 0.151 around a mean of 0.648
limits.what it forbids: the pooled model-vs-rule gap sits inside this spread (Week 6); claim 'not worse, plausibly better'
no seasonality, no algorithm-update period, no repeat measurement

limits.measured as: cpc = 0 on 76% of rows; search_volume = 0 on 37%; sessions_per_click missing on 20%
limits.what it forbids: no monetary value is computed anywhere in this playbook -- the inputs would not carry it
the full ~79M-row release was not used; numbers are of this slice
